correctness.rationale: All quantifiers and cases verified algebraically. With \(a=R-T>0\), \(b=P-S>0\), and \(t=(n-1)b/(a+b)\), a current \(A\) best responder has advantage \((a+b)(k-1-t)\) and current \(B\) has \((a+b)(k-t)\). Across imitating agents the payoffs differ by \((a+b)(k-w)\) with \(w\) strictly between \(t\) and \(t+1\). Thus \(k<h\) only decreases, \(k>h\) only increases, and boundary switches at \(k=h\) increase \(|k-h|\) from zero. Endpoint singleton cases and all ties are explicitly checked. The potential is at most \(n-1\), proving finitely many switches; fairness implies eventual absorption. Exact equilibrium classification and sharpness are shown. Executed standalone integer/rational regression covers 5700 parameter/type cases, 171120 states, 945888 activations. Finite checks are not the infinite proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Existing convergence for all imitators or all best responders does not logically imply convergence for an arbitrary mixture. originality.rationale: The motivating full preprint proves section-count convergence for paths and sparse trees and leaves other graph topologies open. Other inspected published primary models address global/self-inclusive aggregate payoff conventions or pure update rules. Comparisons are statement-level; the present strict hinge potential, exact fair-schedule result, and sharp switching bound were not implied by inspected results, but global publication priority is not certified.
residual_risks: There may exist an unlocated stronger result for homogeneous well-mixed hybrid imitation/BR populations, especially in self-inclusive variants with a transfer argument.

The 2022 mixed aggregate-population paper has wider population classifications, but their precise self-interaction, comparator, and admissibility conventions differ; novelty concerns the exact neighbor-only strict-switch theorem.
2016 and 2021 comparison sources were only partly inspected, as described; they are not decisive sources for the specific mixed process.

value.rationale: The complete graph is the natural dense counterpart of the 2023 sparse-tree open-topology question. A one-dimensional globally strict potential for arbitrary mixtures gives genuinely uniform finite switch complexity and full consensus when at least one BR is present, while exactly classifying exceptional pure-imitator absorbing coexistence. The optimal \(n-1\) switch length exhibits the value of that precise bound, not just code reproducibility.
